comparison: Strong agreement on habituation hallmarks (C4-C8, C60, C62, C66, C69). Both evaluations find the model successfully reproduces key habituation properties. OpenEval emphasizes analytical solutions and simulations; peer reviewers highlight the model's simplicity and biological generality. Peer review also includes C117 (robustness summary) which OpenEval addresses separately in R13.

Strong agreement on mutual information findings (C9, C41, C42). Both evaluations support that information gain peaks at intermediate habituation levels. OpenEval focuses on computational verification; peer reviewers emphasize the theoretical interest and wide relevance of this finding. Peer review also includes C119-C120 (Pareto optimization claims) which OpenEval addresses in R3.

Significant disagreement on Pareto optimization generality (C10, C43, C84-C85, C88, C118-C121). OpenEval finds these claims SUPPORTED through analytical derivation and computational verification. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 raising unresolved concerns about generality across parameter regimes and signal strengths. OpenEval includes C119-C120 here while peer review groups them with R2; OpenEval includes C121 separately in R7 while peer review includes it here.

Disagreement on experimental validation (C11, C110, C112-C115, C124). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with qualitative agreement in PCA analysis. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 raising specific methodological concerns about PCA implementation, units, and whether similarity is artificially induced by parameter fitting. These concerns remain unresolved.

Strong agreement on storage mechanism necessity (C97-C99, C102, C104-C105, C107-C108). Both evaluations support the three-unit architecture with timescale separation. OpenEval emphasizes mathematical framework and control simulations; peer reviewers highlight biological generality and applicability across domains.

Agreement on energy-information relationship (C82, C122-C123) but different scope. OpenEval focuses on thermodynamic analysis showing reduced energy flux during habituation. Peer review emphasizes broader conceptual implications for biological systems, including future directions (C144-C145) that OpenEval addresses separately in R11.

Strong agreement on minimal modeling philosophy (C54, C116, C142). Both evaluations support the appropriate level of abstraction. OpenEval emphasizes design principles and timescale importance; peer reviewers affirm the model serves as a valuable starting point with good balance between simplicity and biological realism. OpenEval also includes C53, C55 not addressed by peer review.

Partial overlap on adaptive robustness (C121). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as a computational result showing Pareto front collapse. Peer review includes C121 in broader UNCERTAIN evaluation of Pareto optimization generality, reflecting concerns about robustness across parameter regimes.

Minimal overlap on heuristic interpretations (C90, C92). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED as physical interpretations consistent with optimization results. Peer review includes C90 in UNCERTAIN evaluation of Pareto optimization, but doesn't specifically address the heuristic interpretation claims.

OpenEval addresses detailed balance breaking and thermodynamic cycle (C49-C50) as SUPPORTED through model construction. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically comment on these technical thermodynamic claims.

Partial overlap on speculative claims and future work. OpenEval rates C44-C45, C126, C128-C145 as UNCERTAIN, noting they are extrapolations and research proposals. Peer review includes only C144-C145 in SUPPORTED evaluation emphasizing broader implications, but doesn't address the speculative nature of broader optimality claims (C44) or extensive future directions.

OpenEval addresses extensive background and literature review claims (C1-C3, C12-C40, C46, C57, C59, C109, C125, C127, C131) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation; reviewers did not systematically evaluate background knowledge claims.

Partial overlap on robustness summary (C117). OpenEval addresses this separately as SUPPORTED summary statement, noting need for better quantification. Peer review includes C117 in broader evaluation of habituation hallmarks without specific comment on robustness quantification.
